headline: High-risk pair: open-webui’s broad network/MCP/file access can leak or misroute data into RisingWave workflows, while shared-session state raises prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui explicitly supports MCP, plugins, and shared persistent sessions, so attacker-controlled content can reach its instruction channel. RisingWave is a data-engineering system that may consume upstream outputs, but its profile lacks a direct parser claim; uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF open-webui content is copied into RisingWave jobs, SQL, or pipeline configs without sanitization
IF an MCP tool or plugin returns untrusted text that open-webui forwards as instructions
mitigations: Disable or restrict MCP/plugins for untrusted sources
Separate operator chat sessions from data-pipeline workspaces
Add a manual review step before any generated text is pasted into RisingWave
Use allowlisted tool outputs only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between UI outputs and downstream pipeline inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches API keys, files, documents, and persistent memory and has broad network egress plus cloud/API integrations; RisingWave has no egress, but the pair still creates a one-way leak path from sensitive open-webui context into external services. Because the leakage risk is driven by open-webui’s defaults, this is high.
conditions: IF open-webui is connected to any external API, search, or cloud storage integration
IF sensitive files or API keys are present in open-webui context while those integrations are enabled
mitigations: Remove unused external connectors
Rotate and scope API keys before enabling integrations
Limit open-webui to a local-only backend
Store sensitive files outside the shared workspace
requires-engineering: enforce per-connector data-loss policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui can write local files and mounted volumes and also uses persistent shared sessions; RisingWave is a separate data-engineering system with no declared write surface, so direct write-write conflict is not proven. However, shared mutable resources via files or mounted data volumes make overlap plausible, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mounted volume or shared workspace
IF RisingWave jobs read or write artifacts that open-webui also edits
mitigations: Give each agent a separate directory or volume
Mount shared data read-only where possible
Serialize writes with a lock file or job queue
Keep generated artifacts in per-agent subfolders
requires-engineering: add workspace-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can generate outputs from prompts, documents, and tools, and its persistent sessions can preserve mistaken context; RisingWave is a data-engineering system that could act on those outputs if wired into a pipeline. The pair lacks direct evidence of automatic trust, so medium fits the inferred A-to-B handoff.
conditions: IF RisingWave ingests open-webui-generated text as configuration, SQL, or ETL parameters
IF no validation step checks the generated content before execution
mitigations: Require human approval before execution
Validate generated SQL/config against a schema
Compare outputs against source data before running jobs
Log and diff every handoff between agents
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between generation and execution

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui handles API keys, documents, chat messages, and persistent memory, while RisingWave’s profile gives no residency or retention controls. That mismatch creates a plausible compliance gap for shared data classes, but the evidence does not show a specific regulated dataset, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated or policy-bound data is stored in open-webui and then processed by RisingWave
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the two systems
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between systems
Avoid placing regulated data in open-webui memory or files
Document retention and deletion expectations for both tools
Purge stale chats and artifacts regularly
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across the pair
